# xq

Command-line XML and HTML beautifier and content extractor.

# Features

* Syntax highlighting
* Automatic indentation and formatting
* Automatic pagination
* Node content extraction

# Usage

Format an XML file and highlight the syntax:

```
xq test/data/xml/unformatted.xml
```

`xq` also accepts input through `stdin`:

```
curl -s https://www.w3schools.com/xml/note.xml | xq
```

HTML content can be formatted and highlighted as well (using `-m` flag):

```
xq -m test/data/html/formatted.html
```

It is possible to extract the content using XPath query language.
`-x` parameter accepts XPath expression.

Extract the text content of all nodes with `city` name:

```
cat test/data/xml/unformatted.xml | xq -x //city
```

Extract the value of attribute named `status` and belonging to `user`:

```
cat test/data/xml/unformatted.xml | xq -x /user/@status
```

See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/XPath for details.

It is possible to use CSS selector to extract the content as well:

```
cat test/data/html/unformatted.html | xq -q "body > p"
```

Extract an attribute value instead of node content additional option `--attr` (`-a`) can be used:

```
cat test/data/html/unformatted.html | xq -q "head > script" -a "src"
```

Extract part of HTML with tags (not only text content) using CSS selector:

```
cat test/data/html/unformatted.html | xq -n -q "head"
```

Output the result as JSON:

```
cat test/data/xml/unformatted.xml | xq -j
```

This will output the result in JSON format, preserving the XML structure. The JSON output will be an object where:
- XML elements become object keys
- Attributes are prefixed with "@"
- Text content is stored under "#text" if the element has attributes or child elements
- Repeated elements are automatically converted to arrays
- Elements with only text content are represented as strings

# Installation

For macOS, via Homebrew:
```
brew install xq
```

For macOS, via MacPorts:
```
sudo port install xq
```

For Linux using custom installer:
```
curl -sSL https://bit.ly/install-xq | sudo bash
```

For Linux using custom installer, changing INSTALL_DIR, without sudo:
```
curl -sSL https://bit.ly/install-xq | INSTALL_DIR=$(pwd) bash
```

For Ubuntu 22.10 or higher via package manager:
```
apt-get install xq
```

For Fedora via package manager:
```
dnf install xq
```

A more detailed list of Linux distros that package the `xq` utility can be found here:
https://repology.org/project/xq-sibprogrammer/versions

# Options

**--version** | **-v**
Prints version information and exits.

**--help** | **-h**
Prints the synopsis and a list of options and exits.

**--indent** int
Uses the given number of spaces for indentation (default 2).

**--color** | **-c**
Forces colorful output.

**--no-color**
Disables colorful output (only formatting).

**--tab**
Uses tabs instead of spaces for indentation.

**--xpath** | **-x** string
Extracts the node(s) from XML using provided XPath query.

**--extract** | **-e** string
Extracts a single node from XML using provided XPath query.

**--query** | **-q** string
Extracts the node(s) using CSS selector.

**--attr** | **-a** string
Extracts an attribute value instead of node content for provided CSS query.

**--html** | **-m**
Uses HTML formatter instead of XML.

**--json** | **-j**
Output the result as JSON.

**--node** | **-n**
Returns the node content instead of text.

**--in-place** | **-i**
Formats the file in place.
</output>

.\" Manpage for xq utility
.TH XQ 1 "06 Nov 2022" "" "xq man page"
.SH NAME
xq - command-line XML and HTML beautifier and content extractor
.SH SYNOPSIS
xq [\fIoptions...\fR] [\fIfile\fR]
.SH DESCRIPTION
Formats the provided \fIfile\fR and outputs it in the colorful mode.
The file can be provided as an argument or via stdin.
.SH OPTIONS
.PP
\fB--version\fR | \fB-v\fR
.RS 4
Prints versions information and exits.
.RE
.PP
\fB--help\fR | \fB-h\fR
.RS 4
Prints the synopsis and a list of options and exits.
.RE
.PP
\fB--indent\fR \fIint\fR
.RS 4
Uses the given number of spaces for indentation (default 2).
.RE
.PP
\fB--color\fR | \fB-c\fR
.RS 4
Forces colorful output.
.RE
.PP
\fB--no-color\fR
.RS 4
Disables colorful output (only formatting).
.RE
.PP
\fB--tab\fR
.RS 4
Uses tabs instead of spaces for indentation.
.RE
.PP
\fB--xpath\fR | \fB-x\fR \fIstring\fR
.RS 4
Extracts the node(s) from XML using provided XPath query.
.RE
.PP
\fB--extract\fR | \fB-e\fR \fIstring\fR
.RS 4
Extracts a single node from XML using provided XPath query.
.RE
.PP
\fB--query\fR | \fB-q\fR \fIstring\fR
.RS 4
Extracts the node(s) using CSS selector.
.RE
.PP
\fB--attr\fR | \fB-a\fR \fIstring\fR
.RS 4
Extracts an attribute value instead of node content for provided CSS query.
.RE
.PP
\fB--html\fR | \fB-m\fR
.RS 4
Uses HTML formatter instead of XML.
.RE
.PP
\fB--json\fR | \fB-j\fR
.RS 4
Output the result as JSON.
.RE
.PP
\fB--node\fR | \fB-n\fR
.RS 4
Returns the node content instead of text.
.RE
.PP
\fB--in-place\fR | \fB-i\fR
.RS 4
Formats the file in place.
.RE
.SH EXAMPLES
.PP
Format an XML file and highlight the syntax:

.RS 4
$ xq test/data/xml/unformatted.xml
.RE
.PP
Utility also accepts input through stdin:

.RS 4
$ curl -s https://www.w3schools.com/xml/note.xml | xq
.RE
.PP
HTML content can be formatted and highlighted using -m flag:

.RS 4
$ xq -m test/data/html/formatted.html
.RE
.PP
Extract the text content of all nodes with city name:

.RS 4
$ cat test/data/xml/unformatted.xml | xq -x //city
.RE
.PP
Extract the XML content of all nodes with city name:

.RS 4
$ cat test/data/xml/unformatted.xml | xq -n -x //city
.RE
.SH SEE ALSO
.PP
\fBhttps://github.com/sibprogrammer/xq\fR - official website
</output>

package cmd

import (
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "os"
    "xq/internal/formatter"

    "flag"
)

var (
    flagVersion  bool
    flagHelp     bool
    flagIndent   int
    flagColor    bool
    flagNoColor  bool
    flagTab      bool
    flagXPath    string
    flagExtract  string
    flagQuery    string
    flagAttr     string
    flagHTML     bool
    flagJSON     bool
    flagNode     bool
    flagInPlace  bool
    flagCompact  bool
    flagDepth    int
)

func Execute() error {
    fs := flag.NewFlagSet("xq", flag.ContinueOnError)
    fs.Usage = func() {} // We handle help ourselves
    
    fs.BoolVar(&flagVersion, "version", false, "Print version information")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagVersion, "v", false, "Print version information")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagHelp, "help", false, "Print this help message")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagHelp, "h", false, "Print this help message")
    fs.IntVar(&flagIndent, "indent", 2, "Use the given number of spaces for indentation")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagColor, "color", false, "Force colorful output")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagColor, "c", false, "Force colorful output")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagNoColor, "no-color", false, "Disable colorful output")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagTab, "tab", false, "Use tabs for indentation")
    fs.StringVar(&flagXPath, "xpath", "", "Extract the node(s) from XML")
    fs.StringVar(&flagXPath, "x", "", "Extract the node(s) from XML")
    fs.StringVar(&flagExtract, "extract", "", "Extract a single node from XML")
    fs.StringVar(&flagExtract, "e", "", "Extract a single node from XML")
    fs.StringVar(&flagQuery, "query", "", "Extract the node(s) using CSS selector")
    fs.StringVar(&flagQuery, "q", "", "Extract the node(s) using CSS selector")
    fs.StringVar(&flagAttr, "attr", "", "Extract an attribute value instead of node content for provided CSS query")
    fs.StringVar(&flagAttr, "a", "", "Extract an attribute value instead of node content for provided CSS query")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagHTML, "html", false, "Use HTML formatter")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagHTML, "m", false, "Use HTML formatter")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagJSON, "json", false, "Output the result as JSON")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagJSON, "j", false, "Output the result as JSON")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagNode, "node", false, "Return the node content instead of text")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagNode, "n", false, "Return the node content instead of text")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagInPlace, "in-place", false, "Format file in place")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagInPlace, "i", false, "Format file in place")
    fs.BoolVar(&flagCompact, "compact", false, "Compact JSON output (no indentation)")
    fs.IntVar(&flagDepth, "depth", -1, "Maximum nesting depth for JSON output (-1 for unlimited)")
    fs.IntVar(&flagDepth, "d", -1, "Maximum nesting depth for JSON output (-1 for unlimited)")

    if err := fs.Parse(os.Args[1:]); err != nil {
        return err
    }

    if flagHelp {
        printHelp()
        return nil
    }

    if flagVersion {
        fmt.Println("xq version 1.4.0")
        return nil
    }

    args := fs.Args()
    
    var reader io.Reader
    var filename string
    
    if len(args) > 0 {
        filename = args[0]
        f, err := os.Open(filename)
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("Error: %v", err)
        }
        defer f.Close()
        reader = f
    } else {
        reader = os.Stdin
    }

    opts := formatter.Options{
        Indent:   flagIndent,
        Color:    flagColor,
        NoColor:  flagNoColor,
        Tab:      flagTab,
        XPath:    flagXPath,
        Extract:  flagExtract,
        Query:    flagQuery,
        Attr:     flagAttr,
        HTML:     flagHTML,
        JSON:     flagJSON,
        Node:     flagNode,
        Compact:  flagCompact,
        Depth:    flagDepth,
    }

    var writer io.Writer = os.Stdout
    var tmpFile *os.File

    if flagInPlace && filename != "" {
        var err error
        tmpFile, err = os.CreateTemp("", "xq-*")
        if err != nil {
            return fmt.Errorf("Error: %v", err)
        }
        defer os.Remove(tmpFile.Name())
        writer = tmpFile
    }

    var err error
    if flagHTML || flagQuery != "" || flagAttr != "" {
        err = formatter.FormatHTML(reader, writer, opts)
    } else {
        err = formatter.FormatXML(reader, writer, opts)
    }
    
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    if flagInPlace && filename != "" && tmpFile != nil {
        tmpFile.Close()
        content, readErr := os.ReadFile(tmpFile.Name())
        if readErr != nil {
            return readErr
        }
        return os.WriteFile(filename, content, 0644)
    }

    return nil
}

func printHelp() {
    fmt.Println("Command-line XML and HTML beautifier and content extractor")
    fmt.Println()
    fmt.Println("Usage:")
    fmt.Println("  xq [flags]")
    fmt.Println()
    fmt.Println("Flags:")
    fmt.Println("  -a, --attr string      Extract an attribute value instead of node content for provided CSS query")
    fmt.Println("  -c, --color            Force colorful output")
    fmt.Println("      --compact          Compact JSON output (no indentation)")
    fmt.Println("  -d, --depth int        Maximum nesting depth for JSON output (-1 for unlimited) (default -1)")
    fmt.Println("  -e, --extract string   Extract a single node from XML")
    fmt.Println("  -h, --help             Print this help message")
    fmt.Println("  -m, --html             Use HTML formatter")
    fmt.Println("  -i, --in-place         Format file in place")
    fmt.Println("      --indent int       Use the given number of spaces for indentation (default 2)")
    fmt.Println("  -j, --json             Output the result as JSON")
    fmt.Println("      --no-color         Disable colorful output")
    fmt.Println("  -n, --node             Return the node content instead of text")
    fmt.Println("  -q, --query string     Extract the node(s) using CSS selector")
    fmt.Println("      --tab              Use tabs for indentation")
    fmt.Println("  -v, --version          Print version information")
    fmt.Println("  -x, --xpath string     Extract the node(s) from XML")
}

func NewEncoder(w io.Writer) *Encoder {
	e := &Encoder{printer{w: bufio.NewWriter(w)}}
	e.p.encoder = e
	return e
}

// Indent sets the encoder to generate XML in which each element

func (enc *Encoder) Indent(prefix, indent string) {

	enc.p.indent = indent
}

func (enc *Encoder) Encode(v any) error {

// Another common strategy is to use repeated calls to e.EncodeToken
// to generate the XML output one token at a time.
// The sequence of encoded tokens must make up zero or more valid
// XML elements.
type Marshaler interface {
	MarshalXML(e *Encoder, start StartElement) error
}

// MarshalerAttr is the interface implemented by objects that can marshal
// themselves into valid XML attributes.
//
// MarshalXMLAttr returns an XML attribute with the encoded value of the receiver.
// Using name as the attribute name is not required, but doing so
// will enable Unmarshal to match the attribute to the correct
// struct field.
// If MarshalXMLAttr returns the zero attribute Attr{}, no attribute
// will be generated in the output.
// MarshalXMLAttr is used only for struct fields with the
// "attr" option in the field tag.
type MarshalerAttr interface {
	MarshalXMLAttr(name Name) (Attr, error)
}

// MarshalIndent works like Marshal, but each XML element begins on a new
// indented line that starts with prefix and is followed by one or more
// copies of indent according to the nesting depth.
func MarshalIndent(v any, prefix, indent string) ([]byte, error) {
	var b bytes.Buffer
	enc := NewEncoder(&b)
	enc.Indent(prefix, indent)
	if err := enc.Encode(v); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if err := enc.Close(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

# - "/>" : self-closing (from EndElement(root))
# - "\n" : final newline (from goroutine? or EndElement?)

# So: root.pendingClose is STILL true after PI
# When StartElement(child) is processed:
# - root.pendingClose=true -> write ">" (closing root's start tag, but now it's on the wrong line!)
# - write "\n  " (newline + indent for child)

# So the output is: ...<?pi?>\n>\n  <child/>...
# The "\n" is from the PI, then ">" is the pending close of root, then "\n  " is from child's indent

# 1. PI writes "<?pi?>" + "\n"
# 2. StartElement(child) processes:
#    - root.pendingClose=true -> write ">" (NOW it's written)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
xq - Command-line XML and HTML beautifier and content extractor
"""

import sys
import os
import re
import json
import argparse
from io import StringIO
from xml.etree import ElementTree as ET
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ETree
from html.parser import HTMLParser

VERSION = "1.4.0"

# ANSI color codes
YELLOW = "\033[33m"
GREEN = "\033[32m"
BLUE = "\033[94m"
RESET = "\033[0m"


def is_whitespace_only(s):
    return s.strip() == ""


def trim_trailing_spaces(s):
    """Remove only trailing ASCII spaces (not tabs, newlines, etc.)"""
    return s.rstrip(' ')


def needs_cdata(s):
    return '&' in s or '<' in s


# ============================================================
# XML Tree Parser using xml.sax
# ============================================================

class XMLNode:
    """Represents an XML node"""
    def __init__(self, name, attrs=None, parent=None):
        self.name = name
        self.attrs = attrs or {}  # ordered dict of name -> value
        self.children = []
        self.text = ""
        self.parent = parent
        self.is_comment = False
        self.comment_text = ""
        self.is_pi = False
        self.pi_target = ""
        self.pi_inst = ""
    
    @classmethod
    def comment(cls, text, parent=None):
        node = cls("#comment", parent=parent)
        node.is_comment = True
        node.comment_text = text
        return node
    
    @classmethod
    def pi(cls, target, inst, parent=None):
        node = cls("#pi", parent=parent)
        node.is_pi = True
        node.pi_target = target
        node.pi_inst = inst
        return node


class XMLParser:
    """Custom XML parser that preserves order and handles namespaces"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.root = XMLNode("#document")
        self.stack = [self.root]
        self.ns_map = {}  # URI -> prefix
        self.ns_stack = [{}]  # stack of URI -> prefix maps
    
    def parse(self, content):
        """Parse XML content and return the document root"""
        import xml.parsers.expat as expat
        
        p = expat.ParserCreate()
        p.StartElementHandler = self._start_element
        p.EndElementHandler = self._end_element
        p.CharacterDataHandler = self._char_data
        p.ProcessingInstructionHandler = self._pi
        p.CommentHandler = self._comment
        p.StartNamespaceDeclHandler = self._start_ns
        p.EndNamespaceDeclHandler = self._end_ns
        p.buffer_text = True
        p.returns_unicode = True
        
        try:
            p.Parse(content, True)
        except expat.ExpatError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"XML parse error: {e}")
        
        return self.root
    
    def _start_ns(self, prefix, uri):
        if len(self.ns_stack) > 0:
            self.ns_stack[-1][uri] = prefix if prefix else ""
    
    def _end_ns(self, prefix):
        pass
    
    def _start_element(self, name, attrs_dict):
        self.ns_stack.append({})
        
        # Resolve namespace in element name
        tag = self._resolve_name(name)
        
        # Convert attrs
        attrs = {}
        for k, v in attrs_dict.items():
            resolved_k = self._resolve_attr_name(k)
            attrs[resolved_k] = v
        
        parent = self.stack[-1]
        node = XMLNode(tag, attrs, parent)
        parent.children.append(node)
        self.stack.append(node)
    
    def _end_element(self, name):
        if len(self.stack) > 1:
            self.stack.pop()
        self.ns_stack.pop()
    
    def _char_data(self, data):
        parent = self.stack[-1]
        if is_whitespace_only(data):
            return
        trimmed = trim_trailing_spaces(data)
        parent.text += trimmed
    
    def _pi(self, target, data):
        parent = self.stack[-1]
        node = XMLNode.pi(target, data, parent)
        parent.children.append(node)
    
    def _comment(self, data):
        parent = self.stack[-1]
        node = XMLNode.comment(data, parent)
        parent.children.append(node)
    
    def _get_prefix_for_uri(self, uri):
        """Get namespace prefix for a URI"""
        for ns_frame in reversed(self.ns_stack):
            if uri in ns_frame:
                return ns_frame[uri]
        return None
    
    def _resolve_name(self, name):
        """Resolve a namespace-qualified name to prefix:local format"""
        # expat returns "{uri}local" or just "local"
        if name.startswith("{"):
            uri_end = name.index("}")
            uri = name[1:uri_end]
            local = name[uri_end+1:]
            prefix = self._get_prefix_for_uri(uri)
            if prefix is not None:
                if prefix == "":
                    return local
                return f"{prefix}:{local}"
            else:
                return f"{uri}:{local}"
        return name
    
    def _resolve_attr_name(self, name):
        """Resolve attribute name"""
        if name.startswith("{"):
            uri_end = name.index("}")
            uri = name[1:uri_end]
            local = name[uri_end+1:]

                return f"{prefix}:{local}"
            else:

            return None
        
        def resolve_name(name):
            if name.startswith("{"):
                uri_end = name.index("}")
                uri = name[1:uri_end]
                local = name[uri_end+1:]
                prefix = get_prefix_for_uri(uri)
                if prefix is not None:
                    return f"{prefix}:{local}" if prefix else local
                return f"{uri}:{local}"
            return name
        
        def on_start_ns(prefix, uri):
            ns_stack[-1][uri] = prefix if prefix else ""
        
        def on_end_ns(prefix):
            pass
        
        def on_start_element(name, attrs_dict):
            nonlocal last_was_element
            
            ns_stack.append({})
            depth = len(stack)
            
            if depth > 0:
                parent = stack[-1]
                if parent["pending_close"]:
                    write_pending_close()
                    parent["pending_close"] = False
                out.write(f"\n{indent_str * depth}")
                parent["has_elements"] = True
                parent["has_content"] = True
            
            tag = resolve_name(name)
            write_start_tag_open(tag)
            
            for k, v in attrs_dict.items():
                attr_name = resolve_name(k)
                write_attr(attr_name, v)
            
            stack.append({
                "name": tag,
                "pending_close": True,
                "has_content": False,
                "has_elements": False,
            })
            last_was_element = False
        
        def on_end_element(name):
            nonlocal last_was_element
            
            if not stack:
                return
            
            elem = stack.pop()
            ns_stack.pop()
            depth = len(stack)
            
            if elem["pending_close"]:
                write_self_close()
            elif elem["has_elements"] and last_was_element:
                out.write(f"\n{indent_str * depth}")
                write_end_tag(elem["name"])
            elif elem["has_content"]:
                write_end_tag(elem["name"])
            else:
                # Bug: wrote ">" (from comment) but no proper content
                write_self_close()
            
            last_was_element = True
        
        def on_char_data(data):
            nonlocal last_was_element
            
            if is_whitespace_only(data):
                return
            trimmed = trim_trailing_spaces(data)
            
            if stack:
                parent = stack[-1]
                if parent["pending_close"]:
                    write_pending_close()
                    parent["pending_close"] = False
                parent["has_content"] = True
            
            if needs_cdata(trimmed):
                out.write(f"<![CDATA[{trimmed}]]>")
            else:
                out.write(trimmed)
            
            last_was_element = False
        
        def on_pi(target, data):
            nonlocal last_was_element
            # PI processing: does NOT close parent's pending ">"
            # This is the original behavior (bug)
            try:
                write_pi(target, data)
                out.write("\n")
            except (ValueError, IndexError):
                # Simulate the original panic behavior
                # The partial output is already written
                raise SystemExit(2)
            last_was_element = False
        
        def on_comment(data):
            nonlocal last_was_element
            
            depth = len(stack)
            
            if depth > 0:
                parent = stack[-1]
                if parent["pending_close"]:
                    write_pending_close()
                    parent["pending_close"] = False
                out.write(f"\n{indent_str * depth}")
                # NOTE: do NOT set parent has_content (bug in original)
            
            write_comment(data)
            last_was_element = False
        
        p = expat.ParserCreate()
        p.StartElementHandler = on_start_element
        p.EndElementHandler = on_end_element
        p.CharacterDataHandler = on_char_data
        p.ProcessingInstructionHandler = on_pi
        p.CommentHandler = on_comment
        p.StartNamespaceDeclHandler = on_start_ns
        p.EndNamespaceDeclHandler = on_end_ns
        p.buffer_text = True
        p.returns_unicode = True
        
        try:
            p.Parse(content.encode('utf-8') if isinstance(content, str) else content, True)
        except SystemExit:
            raise
        except Exception:
            # Output raw content on parse error
            out.write(content)
            out.write("\n")
            return
        
        # Final newline
        out.write("\n")

# And then format_xml also writes "\n" -> but actually let me check...

# Looking at format_xml: it calls w_self_close() then last_was_element[0]=True
# But w_self_close() doesn't write "\n"
# The "\n" comes from the on_end_element handler

# Wait, the on_end_element writes:
# if elem.pending_close: write_self_close()
# And then: last_was_element[0] = True
# But there's no "\n" written by on_end_element!

# So where does the "\n" come from for "<root/>\n"?
# It must be the final "out.write('\n')" in format_xml!

# But then format_html also has "out.write('\n')" at the end
# AND write_html_node writes "\n" after the closing tag...
# So we get: </html>\n (from write_html_node) + \n (from format_html) = two newlines

# The fix: in format_html, don't write the final extra "\n"
# OR: write_html_node shouldn't write "\n"

# Let me check what format_xml actually does:
# The final on_end_element for the root element writes:
# w_end_tag(elem["name"]) -> no newline
# But wait, the closing tag itself doesn't have a newline...
# The newline comes from the PARENT writing "\n" before its closing tag
# OR from format_xml's final out.write("\n")

# Actually wait: for XML output with nesting, the PARENT writes "\n" + indent before </parent>
# That writes the newline BEFORE the closing tag, not after
# And then the closing tag itself is written without newline
# Then format_xml writes the FINAL "\n"

# So for "<root/>": 
# on_start_element writes "<root" (pending)
# on_end_element: writes "/>" (self-close)
# format_xml writes "\n"
# Result: "<root/>\n" ✓

# For "<root><child/></root>":
# "<root" (pending)
# "\n  " (before child start)
# "<child" (pending)
# "/>" (child self-close)
# "\n" + "" + "</root>" (parent end, depth=0 so no indent)
# "\n" (final)
# Result: "<root>\n  <child/>\n</root>\n" ✓

# OK so for XML, the nesting works correctly.
# For HTML, I'm writing "\n" AFTER each closing tag in write_html_node
# This means: </html>\n from write_html_node + \n from format_html = two newlines

# Fix: remove the final out.write("\n") from format_html

# Actually wait, let me look at what the XML formatter does for HTML
# The XML formatter writes "\n" at the END (final newline)
# The HTML nodes themselves don't write a trailing newline (they write "\n" after content)
# Hmm, let me re-examine:

# In XML format_xml:
# Each on_end_element writes the closing tag WITHOUT newline
# The "\n" is written by the NEXT sibling's start element (as prefix)
# OR by the parent's end element (when it writes "\n" + indent before the closing tag)
# OR by the final out.write("\n")

# So the LAST element in the XML tree doesn't get a "\n" from any sibling/parent
# It gets its "\n" from the final out.write("\n")

# For HTML, I'm writing "\n" INSIDE write_html_node (after each closing tag)
# This means EVERY closing tag gets a "\n"
# Including the last one (</html>)
# And THEN format_html adds another "\n"

# The fix: DON'T write the final "\n" in format_html
# OR: write write_html_node without the trailing "\n" (like the XML formatter does)
# and have format_html add the final "\n"

# But the HTML formatter structure is different - each node writes its own content
# plus its children recursively
# The nested structure means the final "\n" comes from the last child's "\n"

# For the HTML formatter to match the original, I need to make it write exactly one "\n" at the end
# The simplest fix: remove the final out.write("\n") from format_html

sed -i 's/^    out.write("\\n")/    # Final newline not needed - write_html_node handles it/' /workspace/xq_impl.py

# Wait, that might break the XML formatter. Let me be more careful.
# I need to only fix the HTML formatter

grep -n "out.write" /workspace/xq_impl.py | head -30

# The original panics and outputs ONLY "<?foo" (not "<?foo?>")
# My implementation outputs the full "<?foo?>" before seeing the issue

# I need to reproduce the exact behavior:
# 1. Write "<?foo" (the start of the PI - target only, no "?>")
# 2. Then try to process the empty inst -> panic (exit 2)
# 3. The partial output "<?foo" is already written to stdout
# 4. The panic message goes to stderr

# The key insight: the original writes "<?target" BEFORE trying to parse the inst
# My current implementation writes the FULL PI including "?>" if inst processing succeeds
# For empty inst, I'm skipping the tokens loop, so it still writes "?>"

# I need to restructure the w_pi function to write target FIRST, THEN try to process inst

# Let me update the w_pi function to:
# 1. Write "<?target" immediately (NO "?>")
# 2. Try to process each token
# 3. If a token has no "=", exit with code 2
# 4. After processing all tokens, write "?>"

# Also, for the empty inst case, it should be:
# tokens = "".split(" ") = [""]
# for tok in [""]
#   if not tok: continue -> skip
# This skips all tokens and writes "?>"
# BUT the original panics for empty inst!

# Actually, let me re-read the Go code behavior:

# The issue: on_pi writes to `out` (via the closure)
# Then ExpatError is raised
# Then the error handler writes the raw content again
# Then format_xml adds the final "\n"

# I need to track whether any output has been written
# and if so, don't write the raw content fallback

# But the problem is: some VALID XML with just a PI (no root element) 
# should still be handled somehow

# Looking at the original behavior:
# "<?pi foo=bar?>" (PI at top level, no root element)
# -> Go's encoding/xml would parse this as a ProcInst token
# -> Then get EOF without a root element
# -> The formatter outputs the PI and exits

# My Python implementation:
# -> on_pi callback writes the PI
# -> Then expat raises error because no root element
# -> Then the error handler kicks in

# The fix: Don't write raw content if we're in the middle of processing
# One way: track if we've already written some output
# Another way: tolerate the "no element found" error

# Actually, looking at the original behavior:
# The original processes tokens sequentially until EOF
# If there's no root element, it still processes whatever tokens came before EOF
# The "ExpatError: no element found" is expat being strict

# For Go's encoding/xml, parsing a standalone PI without a root element WORKS
# because xml.Decoder reads tokens lazily and doesn't require a root element

# I need to make the Python expat more lenient
# One approach: parse in chunks and stop on the "no element found" error
# Another approach: wrap the content in a dummy root element for parsing

# Actually, the simplest fix: when we get ExpatError "no element found",
# DON'T write raw content (because we already processed the PI via callbacks)
# Just add the final newline

# Let me update the error handler:
sed -n '234,240p' /workspace/xq_impl.py

# The output matches the expected format ✓
# The ">" is on a separate line because:
# 1. PI writes <?pi foo=bar?> + "\n"
# 2. When StartElement(child) is processed, parent.pending_close=True
# 3. parent.pending_close -> write ">" then newline+indent
# 4. ">" appears on a line by itself (because the PI already wrote "\n")
# 5. Then "\n  " (which is from the "\n" + indent before the child)

# Wait, that gives ">\n  <child>" but the output shows ">\n  <child/>"
# Let me re-check the od output:

echo '<root><?pi foo=bar?><child/></root>' | /workspace/executable --no-color | od -An -c

# Everything looks good! Let me commit

cd /workspace
git add .gitignore compile.sh xq_impl.py
git commit -m "Implement xq - XML/HTML beautifier and content extractor

Reimplementation of xq v1.4.0 in Python 3.

Features:
- XML formatting with proper indentation and syntax highlighting
- HTML formatting with CSS selector support
- XPath extraction from XML documents
- JSON output from XML data
- All original flags supported (--color, --no-color, --tab, --indent, etc.)
- Original bugs reproduced (comment-only element -> />, PI panic for invalid inst)

Implementation:
- Uses Python's xml.parsers.expat for XML tokenization
- Uses Python's html.parser for HTML parsing
- Custom XPath evaluator supporting //path, /path, @attr, predicates, functions
- Custom CSS selector parser supporting >, descendant, class, id selectors

def write_html_node(out, node, depth, indent_str, color):
    """Write formatted HTML node"""
    indent = indent_str * depth
    
    if node.is_doctype:
        out.write(f"<!{node.doctype_data}>\n")
        return
    
    if node.is_comment:
        if color:
            out.write(f"{BLUE}<!--{RESET}{BLUE}{node.comment_text}{RESET}{BLUE}-->{RESET}\n")
        else:
            out.write(f"<!--{node.comment_text}-->\n")
        return
    
    if color:
        out.write(f"{YELLOW}<{node.tag}{RESET}")
    else:
        out.write(f"<{node.tag}")
    
    for name, value in (node.attrs or []):
        if color:
            if value is not None:
                out.write(f' {name}{GREEN}="{value}"{RESET}')
            else:
                out.write(f' {name}')
        else:
            if value is not None:
                out.write(f' {name}="{value}"')
            else:
                out.write(f' {name}')
    
    is_void = node.tag.lower() in HTML_VOID_ELEMENTS
    has_children = bool(node.children)

        out.write("\n")

        if color:

        else:
            out.write(f"></{node.tag}>")
        out.write("\n")

        if color:
            out.write(f"{YELLOW}>{RESET}{node.text}{YELLOW}</{node.tag}>{RESET}")
        else:
            out.write(f">{node.text}</{node.tag}>")
        out.write("\n")
